page: Amazon Web Services m5d.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The system provides 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 3600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. While single-core metrics from stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom 25%, its multi-core capabilities are strong, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached and uncached large block operations scoring in the top 25%. Redis SET operations also demonstrate strong performance, executing 74.41 million operations per second. However, text generation speeds for large language models are poor, falling into the bottom 10%.

From a resource density perspective, the m5d.24xlarge offers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio combined with high-capacity local NVMe storage. This hardware profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high-throughput local scratch space and parallel processing without the premium of memory-optimized classes. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, caching layers like Redis, and general-purpose enterprise workloads that benefit from high multi-core density and fast local storage.
